plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction (Vickrey auction), bidding your true value is a dominant strategy. This holds regardless of the number of bidders or their strategies, since your payment depends only on the second-highest bid, not your own bid. Bidding above value risks overpaying; bidding below value risks losing profitable wins. Therefore, the optimal action is to bid exactly my private value of $34, ensuring maximum expected profit given the auction mechanics.

This is a second-price (Vickrey) auction with 3 bidders and independent private values. In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what others do - it maximizes expected profit. Bidding higher risks overpaying if I win; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Since my value is $28, I should bid exactly $28 to ensure optimal outcomes in both winning and losing scenarios.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy. This holds regardless of other bidders' strategies, since paying only the second-highest bid means you cannot benefit from bidding above or below your true valuation. Therefore, the optimal action is to bid exactly $14, my private value, to maximize expected profit.
